messages:
Devin: Quick sync — we need to finalize the plan for the retention SLA migration + evidence export for SOC2 v2. Legal has pushed for a 7yr archival path and customers keep asking for per-tenant TTLs and legal-hold. Can we scope an MVP for Q2 that satisfies auditability without blowing cost?

Samir: High level — agree on per-tenant TTL, legal-hold flag, and an immutable audit export. Biggest risks: backfill cost and query load during deletes. HSM-wrapped exports for every object is expensive. Recommend HSM for exported keys, not per-object crypto in MVP.

Claudia: From legal: 7yrs is fine but audit artifacts must include request metadata + decision rationale (who/why). Exports must be verifiable (signatures) and include retention-policy version. Also we need a documented legal-hold override that prevents deletes.

Alex: Infra note — deletions need to be batched and idempotent. Backfill across large tenants will need throttles and backlog consumer. Also want to expose per-tenant retention size metrics for billing/alerts.

Priya: Oncall/ops: need a migration runbook, canary rollout plan, and a rollback path (replay tombstones). If we do per-tenant retention, add a safety net: soft-delete window (30 days) before permanent purge.

Samir: Proposed MVP scope (quick list):
```
- Per-tenant retention TTL UI + API (tenant-admin only)
- Legal-hold flag that prevents purge and marks events as "preserved"
- Soft-delete pipeline: tombstone -> 30d grace -> permanent delete job (batched)
- Immutable audit log entries exported in ndjson with signed manifest (key stored in HSM)
- Export to customer-controlled S3 for enterprise customers (encrypt with KMS/HSM-wrapped key)
- Backfill tool that migrates existing data into new retention buckets with throttling
```

Claudia: Schema requirements for exports: include actor id, api_key_id, request_id, timestamp, model, prompt hash, retention_policy_id, legal_hold_flag, rationale. Exports must be indexed for sampling during audits.

Devin: Tradeoffs we discussed:
- Full HSM per-object: strongest guarantee, very high cost -> defer to Phase 2 for cold-archive per-object wrapping.
- MVP HSM-wrapped manifest/key: good compromise (signed manifest + HSM key to sign).
- Backfill window: 30d rolling is safest but long runs cost more; can we offer an accelerated paid backfill for large customers?

Alex: Implementation constraints:
- DB: Add retention_policy_id to primary event table, backfill sets policy and writes tombstones for expired rows.
- Delete job: consumer reads tombstones, deletes in shards, writes audit export pointer.
- Export: create signed manifest -> upload to S3 -> store manifest hash in audit-log index.

Priya: Launch / QA criteria suggestion:
1) End-to-end: set retention on test tenant -> ingest -> soft-delete -> permanent delete -> manifest visible in audit index.
2) Export verification: signed manifest verified against HSM public key (compliance-bot test).
3) Load: deletion pipeline sustains Xk deletes/min without impacting front-line latency.
4) Legal review: export schema approved by CLO.
5) Runbook + rollback tested for backfill.

compliance-bot: SOC2 checklist updated: added "retention-policy-config", "legal-hold", "signed-export-manifest". See https://internal.redwood/compliance/soc2-v2 (doc stub).

Samir: Open questions:
- Should per-tenant retention default to org-level policy or account-level opt-in? (defaults matter for risk)
- How to present retention to customers in Console (simple slider vs advanced JSON)?

Claudia: Legal preference: default to conservative (retention off by default, unless customer agrees or sales contract says otherwise). But for enterprise we can push default to 7yrs if specified in contract. Need explicit consent.

Devin: Proposal/decision draft:
- MVP scope includes everything in Samir's list but with HSM used for signing manifests only.
- Backfill will run in phased waves with a 30d soft-delete grace and throttled permanent delete.
- Default retention: off; enterprises can opt into contract-backed defaults.
- Phase 2: per-object HSM wrapping and cold-archive lifecycle automation.

Alex: +1 on phased backfill and manifest signing. Will prototype delete job and measure throughput.

Priya: I'll draft the runbook and canary plan. Suggest canary start = 5 enterprise tenants in region-us-west; monitor delete-latency and CPU.

Claudia: Legal will prepare audit checklist and sample export acceptance criteria.

Devin: Action items (owners & ETA):
- Samir: Spec for export manifest + audit schema (PR by Tue)
- Alex: Prototype delete/backfill job + perf numbers (Weds)
- Priya: Runbook + canary plan (EOD Fri)
- Claudia: Legal checklist + contract language for opt-in defaults (next Tue)
- Devin: Draft launch criteria and OKR mapping (end of week)

Devin: If no objections, I'll mark this as "Q2 retention MVP - approved scope" and open a planning epic. Please add blockers here. :thumbsup:

Samir: One blocker: need HSM access for signing in test env — cc infra.

Alex: Noted — filing infra ticket now.

Priya: Adding tasks to the sprint board.

Claudia: Adding legal review slot.

Devin: Thanks all — feel free to @ me if something needs re-prioritizing.
